title: Return structured validation results from x-llm-req-parameter.validation.function
objective: Let x-llm-req-parameter.validation.function return a well-defined result object whose error entries tell users and agents what is wrong with a parameter and how to fix it, and carry those entries unchanged to library callers and llm req error output. Contract sections: requests/README.md#validation-functions; requests/README.md#schema-declared-files-and-librarycli-boundaries.

branch.name: WI-0025-structured-validation-results
branch.rationale: Each work item is processed on its own branch.

request.text: The validation function should be able to return a well-defined object containing error messages intended to instruct users/agents on how to fix their parameters.

scope.name: result-contract
scope.description: Define a closed validation result object { valid, errors?: [{ message, path?, remediation? }] } with bounded counts and lengths, read without running validator getters.
scope.reason: Validators need a well-defined way to report actionable problems.

scope.name: structured-failure
scope.description: Raise an exported ParameterValidationFailure carrying normalized issues for every validator-driven failure, including the existing false, string, thrown, and rejected-promise forms, and add an optional metadata remediation for false and string returns.
scope.reason: Library callers and agents need machine-readable guidance.

scope.name: cli-output
scope.description: Make llm req emit one JSON error entry per issue with parameterPath and remediation fields.
scope.reason: CLI users and agents must receive the fix-it guidance.

scope.name: documentation-and-compatibility
scope.description: Document the result object, failure type, and error output; keep existing validator return forms and the full provider-free gate green.
scope.reason: The request README is the authoritative llm req contract.

nonGoals.name: aggregate-across-validators
nonGoals.description: Do not change the rule that the first failing validator stops validation; one validator may report several issues.

nonGoals.name: response-envelope
nonGoals.description: Do not change the llm/response/v1 schema, error codes, or non-request commands.
nonGoals.reason: The change is limited to request parameter validation.

nonGoals.name: provider-and-release
nonGoals.description: Do not make authenticated provider calls, publish, deploy, or claim production readiness.

items.name: result-contract
items.description: A validation function may return { valid, errors } where valid is a boolean and each error has a required message and optional path and remediation; malformed results fail closed.
items.reason: The result shape must be well-defined.

acceptanceCriteria.description: valid: true passes; valid: false with 1 to 20 errors fails with those errors; paths default to the validator's concrete path.
Unknown members, wrong types, empty or oversized error lists, valid: true with errors, and accessor properties are configuration errors that never run validator getters.

items.name: structured-failure
items.description: Every validator-driven failure raises an exported ParameterValidationFailure with normalized issues; metadata remediation applies to false and string returns.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Object, false, string, thrown, and rejected-promise failures all yield ParameterValidationFailure issues with path, message, and remediation when supplied.
The failure keeps code CONFIGURATION_INVALID, a bounded summary message, zero provider calls, and is exported from the package entry point.

items.name: cli-output
items.description: llm req emits one JSON error entry per issue with code, phase, message, parameterPath, and remediation when supplied, and exits nonzero.
items.reason: CLI users and agents must receive the guidance.

acceptanceCriteria.description: A multi-issue validator produces matching error entries in order on stderr with exit code 1 and no stdout.
Non-validation failures keep the existing single-entry error shape.

items.name: documentation-and-compatibility
items.description: requests/README.md, the decision log, README.md, and SKILL.md document the result object, failure type, and error output; existing behavior and the full provider-free gate stay green.
items.reason: The contract must match behavior and the change must be additive.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Contract text names every result member, bound, the failure type, and the CLI error fields.
The full repository gate passes, including existing WI-0023 validator tests.
